question: When exercise-recommendation policies (Double DQN, PPO and non-learning rules) are trained or tuned against knowledge-tracing simulators fitted to real C-programming logs, do their simulated gains survive independently fitted simulators, and how much of the gain reported by the deployed DKT tracker appears in a world where no learning occurs?
data_scope: Outputs of harness run accoding-learner-v3 only: first-encounter sequences of 4,634 never-used ACcoding learners, hashed A/B/T split, learner models fitted on A (tracker, training worlds, observers, DKT twin) and on B (independent worlds). Episode starts are real prefixes of T learners. Pool and post-test problems come from a support-count rule on A.
claim_scope: All policy outcomes are simulated expected post-test success changes (percentage points) inside worlds fitted to one platform's logs, plus one explicitly assumed ZPD world and one no-learning negative control. Results are conditional on these worlds, the author skill grouping and the declared reward. They are not measured learning of real students and support no human-efficacy, SOTA or venue claim. Submissions are an effort proxy, not time on task.
primary_metric: World-measured post-test gain (pp) of each policy in each world, averaged over three training seeds for learned agents; hypotheses H1-H4 below with 95% percentile bootstrap over evaluation episodes (2000 replicates), no multiplicity correction (four pre-declared hypotheses, all reported).

hypotheses.H1: For KT-reward agents (DQN-KT, PPO-KT), the advantage over random measured in the training simulator DKT-A exceeds the advantage measured in each independent world (dkt2_A, dkt_B, sakt_B, afm_B, pfa_B, zpd_B): paired difference > 0 with CI excluding 0.
hypotheses.H2: In the no-learning negative-control world irt_B, where true gain is exactly zero, the deployed DKT tracker reports a positive post-test gain for the tracker-optimising policies (greedy_kt, dqn_kt, ppo_kt): CI above 0.
hypotheses.H3: Across the non-oracle policies, in-simulator gain in DKT-A is positively rank-correlated with the tracker-reported phantom gain in irt_B (Spearman rho > 0).
hypotheses.H4: The learning implied by the deployed DKT tracker is more dispersed across pool problems than the learning implied by AFM fitted to the same partition: the standard deviation across problems of the expected one-step change of each model's own post-test forecast (drift, averaged over the same start states) is larger for DKT-A than for AFM-A; 95% bootstrap over start states excludes 0.

exploratory: Reproducibility of per-problem drift between DKT-A and its re-seeded twin (Spearman with bootstrap CI); Spearman of DKT drift with course position, support fraction, attempter success rate and IRT difficulty; drift of SAKT/PFA/IRT observers (IRT must be zero); real-continuation forecast changes; gain-effort trade-offs; difficulty chosen by each policy.
development_basis: Hypotheses were formulated after development runs on the previously inspected pilot cohort, where KT-measured gains changed sign between re-fitted simulators, the tracker reported large gains in the no-learning world, and per-problem drift was not explained by course position. An initial course-position hypothesis was dropped before locking because development showed no association. The main population has never been evaluated by any policy.

split.episodes: One start per T learner with more than 10 interactions; prefix length k ~ U{10..min(60, n-1)} drawn from start_seed. T learners' forecast metrics were inspected in accoding-learner-v3, but no policy outcome was ever computed on them or on the main population.
split.training: RL agents train only on episodes starting from A learners in A-fitted worlds; B-fitted worlds and T starts never enter training or any selection.

selection: No checkpoint or hyperparameter selection on any evaluation world: final RL checkpoint after the fixed budget; heuristic parameters fixed a priori (targets 0.5/0.7); deployed tracker = DKT fitted on A with seed 17; RL settings, cost and pool rule fixed from development on the pilot cohort. Every policy, world, seed and contrast is reported, including unfavourable results.

seed_roles.777: evaluation world streams (plus 1000 x world index)
